subject.title: feat(android): Talk camera flip control and microphone selection

question: Should Android Talk’s persistent camera preference govern generic agent camera captures when the agent omits `facing`, while explicit agent-facing choices continue to override it?
rationale: The PR adds a user-facing persistent control whose intended scope crosses the Android node and the core agent media tool; the intended product contract must be confirmed before changing the established core default behavior.

options.title: Honor the persisted Talk preference
options.body: Preserve omitted `facing` through the core invoke path, retain explicit agent values as overrides, and validate the behavior on a physical Android device.

options.title: Scope the control to a narrower flow
options.body: Keep generic agent camera commands front-facing by default and redesign the Talk control so it affects only an explicitly defined capture workflow.

recommendation.title: Honor the persisted Talk preference
recommendation.body: Preserve omitted `facing` through the core invoke path, retain explicit agent values as overrides, and validate the behavior on a physical Android device.

likelyOwner.reason: The documented Android app owner is best placed to confirm the intended mobile-product contract across Talk UI and node capture behavior.
